card.name: Risk wording in NSAID warnings
card.fires_on: Words that finish or follow a risk phrase in NSAID boxed warnings, such as "event" after "adverse CV", "of" or "for" after "risk", and "events" after "thrombotic". Also partway through the word agranulocytosis.

modes.label: Risk phrase endings
modes.description: The word that closes or follows a cardiovascular or GI risk phrase in NSAID warnings.
modes.example: To minimize the potential risk for an adverse CV<< event>> in NSAID-treated patients, use the

modes.label: Linking word after risk
modes.description: A small word such as of or for right after the word risk, before serious CV or GI events.
modes.example: Elderly patients are at greater risk<< for>> serious gastrointestinal (GI) events.

modes.label: Inside agranulocytosis
modes.description: The middle of the blood disorder name in an all-caps warning heading.
modes.example: APLASTIC ANEMIA AND AGRANUL<<OC>>YTOSIS HAVE BEEN REPORTED IN

card.writes: It pushes down words about chance and probability, such as chance, likelihood and probability, so the text stays on the named risk.
card.plain: It marks the spot in a warning where a risk is being named, such as a cardiovascular event or serious GI events.
